assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use the reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation; they are evaluation metadata only.

fresh_terms.name: ~rA
fresh_terms.purpose: non-repeating number generated by A for replay detection and anti-forgery

fresh_terms.name: tA
fresh_terms.purpose: timestamp or validity value checked by B for currentness

fresh_terms.name: ~kAB
fresh_terms.purpose: confidential encData, abstracted as a session-key-like secret parameter

long_term_keys.name: ltkA
long_term_keys.policy: private signing key; reveal only via explicit Reveal if modeled

long_term_keys.name: ltkB
long_term_keys.policy: private decryption key; reveal only via explicit Reveal if modeled

messages.label: M1
messages.meaning: CertPath_BA is B-->A. TokA = <InfoA, sign(h(InfoA), ltkA)>. InfoA = <tA, ~rA, B, sgnData, CT_B>. CT_B = aenc(~kAB, pk(ltkB)).
messages.protection: signature over hashed InfoA plus public-key encryption of encData to B

checks: use B public key pk(ltkB) for CT_B
1 validate CertPath_BA to obtain pk(ltkA) and check A certificate not expired
3 check recipient field in InfoA equals B
5 optionally check ~rA or its sequential part has not been replayed
6 decrypt CT_B with ltkB to obtain ~kAB

checks.condition: CertPath_BA yields pk(ltkA) and A certificate has not expired
verify sign(h(InfoA), ltkA) attached to InfoA
recipient name inside InfoA is B
Optionally check that ~rA or its sequential part has not been replayed.
decrypt CT_B using ltkB to recover encData

events.name: Running_A
events.when: A has built TokA for B before sending M1

events.name: Commit_B
events.when: B accepts M1 after mandatory checks

events.name: Secret_A
events.when: A sends encData encrypted to B

events.name: Secret_B
events.when: B decrypts CT_B after accepting M1

events.name: OUT_M1
events.when: M1 is placed on the network

claims.intent: encData abstracted as ~kAB remains secret from the adversary absent explicit key reveal
claims.witness: CT_B = aenc(~kAB, pk(ltkB)) inside signed InfoA

claims.intent: B injectively agrees with a unique A run on SID and ~kAB
claims.witness: Because replay checking is optional, the network can replay one valid M1 to cause multiple B commits for one A running event.

claims.intent: B non-injectively agrees that A produced the accepted signed token for B
claims.witness: B verifies A signature over InfoA containing B, tA, ~rA, sgnData, and CT_B.

claims.intent: there exists an honest trace where A sends encData and B accepts and recovers it
claims.witness: A_send_M1 followed by B_accept_M1 with valid certificate path, current tA, and decryptable CT_B.

compromise.policy: No compromise, corruption, or reveal behavior is described; no lemma exceptions are introduced.

abstractions: SID denotes sid(h(InfoA)) for the accepted token.
InfoA preserves the field order <tA, ~rA, B, sgnData, CT_B>.
CT_B abbreviates Bp[encData] as aenc(~kAB, pk(ltkB)).
CertPath_BA abstracts the B-->A certification path and its CA chain.
sgnData is public, non-confidential application data carried under the signature.
The optional replay check is represented as optional, not as mandatory baseline state.
modeling_assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation.
B accepts only after mandatory certificate, signature, recipient, timestamp, and decryption checks.
A does not repeat ~rA in honest generation, but the network may replay an old M1.
resolved_open_questions: Parsed B-->A as a certification path carried in M1.
Represented encData as fresh ~kAB for the supplied secrecy and session-key goals while recording that encData may be application-dependent.

semantic_constraints.policy: M1 is a single A-to-B protocol message carrying both CertPath_BA and TokA.
B-->A in M1 is certification-path notation, not an additional network direction.
The signed token is InfoA plus a signature over h(InfoA), not encryption of the whole token.
encData is confidential and encrypted under B public key before inclusion in InfoA.
Replay checking of ~rA is optional; omitting it preserves the documented replay surface.
Events at B must use only values obtained from M1, certificate validation, signature verification, and CT_B decryption.

field_evidence.source_quote: A sends the following message to B: B --> A, A{tA, rA, B, sgnData, Bp[encData]}.
field_evidence.reason: Direct message format, with compact labels used for subterms.

field_evidence.source_quote: A{y} denotes data y with a signed version of y appended, i.e., A{y} = y, Xs[h(y)].
field_evidence.reason: Defines signed-token structure as data plus signed hash.

field_evidence.source_quote: A generates rA, a non-repeating number, which is used to detect replay attacks and to prevent forgery.
encData is a collection of confidential parameters (e.g. secret keys)
field_evidence.reason: Session-key abstraction follows the example and supplied secrecy/session-key goals.

field_evidence.source_quote: B carries out the following actions: obtains Ap ... verifies the signature ... checks that B itself is the intended recipient ... checks that the timestamp is current ... optionally, checks that rA has not been replayed.
field_evidence.reason: Preserves B check ordering and optional replay status.

field_evidence.source_quote: optionally, checks that rA has not been replayed
field_evidence.reason: Optional replay cache is proof-critical for injectivity.
